Senses.PreferredTarget: Mountains are not mountains; waters are not waters
SearchAliases: mountains are not mountains; waters are not waters
Senses.Note: The line says that mountains are not mountains and waters are not waters. Dabo gives it in two exchanges, once when asked about an earlier teacher and again in response to a monk citing an old saying. Muyun uses it to answer a question about transformation. Tianyin makes it the opening of a challenge verse. Daxiu places it between seeing things as they are and seeing them so again. Faxi draws a circle for the first view, crosses it out for this one, and strikes the table before the return. Miyin warns a patron that seeing appearances as fixed misses the matter. The reversal is a live test, not a settled description of the landscape.

Senses.Explanation: The denial of mountains and waters interrupts a familiar way of naming what is seen. Dabo and Muyun give the line as a direct answer, while Tianyin speaks it in a verse addressed to a patron. Daxiu, Faxi, and Miyin set the reversal beside a return to ordinary mountains and waters.

Senses.Explanation: A mountain master is the monk who heads, occupies, or is identified with a mountain monastery. Sima Toutuo calls Lingyou the future master of Mount Gui; other records call Xiu 'the mountain master' as a standing title. It is an institutional or personal designation, not a claim that the person owns a mountain.

Senses.PreferredTarget: This mountain monk has lost out today
SearchAliases: this mountain monk has lost out today
Senses.Note: Miyun says that if no one can respond to his invitation, he has lost out. Yinyuan says it after a monk stands hesitant despite being struck; Sanshan says it after the assembly has offered answers to his question. Yezhu says it when no one responds, and Huiyue uses it after inviting anyone able to strike him in reply to his judgment of two old masters. The master’s self-deprecating line both ends the immediate test and leaves the missing answer visible. The passages do not force a single verdict on whether he has truly lost.

Senses.Explanation: The master says he has lost out after pressing the audience or a monk for a live answer. Miyun, Yezhu, and Huiyue turn audience silence into an apparent defeat of their own. Yinyuan and Sanshan use the same admission after a monk hesitates or the assembly offers answers that do not settle the matter.

Senses.PreferredTarget: This mountain monk would do otherwise
SearchAliases: this mountain monk would do otherwise
Senses.Note: “This mountain monk would do otherwise” is a hinge in case commentary. Baichi follows it with a new answer to old lines on parents and Buddhas. Tianyin recasts an anniversary memorial as the teacher’s release, and Yunwai proposes a different reply to Subhuti. Xueguan refuses an older medical comparison; Linye rewrites a travel verse; Jifei counters the claim that meeting a fellow traveler ends the journey. The phrase announces an alternative; its content comes in the words or action that follows.

Senses.Note: “This mountain monk is at fault” can sound like an apology, but these exchanges keep the question open. Zhangxue says it after lifting a whisk and asking the assembly to recognize it. Hanyu says it to a monk who cannot name his whisk; Chaozong says it when asked why the master cannot be seen nearby. Lianfeng says it when challenged for falling into words, and Yushan says it when a monk reproaches him as rash. The self-blame redirects the encounter instead of closing it.

Senses.Explanation: A master admits fault just as the listener expects the master to defend the answer. Senses.PreferredTarget: This mountain monk is deaf
Senses.Note: “This mountain monk is deaf” is used as an encounter reply; the records do not prove literal deafness or deliberate pretense. Yangzhuo says it when asked how an unmoving Buddha can be brought, then asks for a louder question. Yinyuan gives it when asked where the bell and drum sound went. Yushan answers a question about a person without hands with the same claim and again asks the monk to speak louder. Each answer keeps the student’s question in the encounter rather than resolving it as a detached proposition.

Entries.SourceTerm: 山前一片閒田地，叉手叮嚀問祖翁

Senses.PreferredTarget: A patch of idle field lies before the mountain; hands folded, I ask the old ancestor again
SearchAliases: a patch of idle field lies before the mountain; hands folded, i ask the old ancestor again
Senses.Note: Wuzu Fayan's verse sets a patch of idle land before the mountain and shows the seeker still asking an ancestor about it. Foyuan asks whether descendants can cultivate this inheritance. Huiyue calls for tending the field, while Pingshi faults the confidence of claiming it as a possession. Tanfang adapts the image when temple land is restored, and Liaotang raises a whisk to question why recognizing what is plain can take so long. The field image holds presence and hesitation together.

Entries.SourceTerm: 山前一片閒田地，叉手叮嚀問祖翁，幾度賣來還自買，為憐松竹引清風

Senses.PreferredTarget: A patch of idle field before the mountain; hands folded, I ask the ancestral elder. Again and again I sell it and buy it back, for love of pines and bamboo drawing a clear breeze
AlternateTargets: Before the mountain lies an unused field; I respectfully ask the ancestor why I keep selling and buying it back to enjoy pines, bamboo, and a clean wind
SearchAliases: Wuzu idle mountain field ancestor sold bought pine bamboo breeze
Wuzu Fayan realization verse field clear wind
Senses.Note: Wuzu Fayan is identified as the speaker of the full realization verse. Guxue challenges it line by line; Baiyu explains the field as present work; Zuliang compares the ancestral field with his own monastery; Yushan tests the verse against the concrete task of feeding the community. These current masters are commentators, while Wuzu owns the quoted words. A shorter public entry contains only the mountain-field opening; the full verse adds the recurring sale and purchase and the pine-bamboo breeze that later masters interpret.

Senses.Explanation: Mountains are mountains and waters are waters states the visible world without exchanging one thing for another. Chan masters sometimes permit that plain distinction after overturning confusion, yet elsewhere immediately challenge it, warn against guarding it, or call it a provisional lowering of the clouds. Shiqi Tongyun permits the formula while keeping before, after, and the present day under examination. Yingning Zhijing quotes an objector who says that such plain distinctions still do not answer what is immediately present. Chaozong Tongren places the restored distinctions after a great death and before further forging under the hammer. Tian’an Sheng returns to east as east and west as west after a cosmic disorientation, then tells the assembly they still do not know. Baichi Xingyuan states each class in its place, calls that a lowering of the clouds, and refuses to rest content with it.

AlternateTargets: A silver mountain moon draws an elder out, and an unhurried walk carries him past the western ridge

Senses.Note: A silver-bright mountain moon draws out an elder's interest, and his idle walk carries him beyond the peak before he notices. Miyun puts the pair in his own verse; Linye uses it to answer a question about freedom. Eryin and Yezhu give it after contrasting old responses or asking what the assembly understands. The lack of self-conscious itinerary is as important as the moonlit scenery.

Senses.Explanation: Mountains and waters is the paired noun for a landscape considered as its mountains and waters. In Complete Five Lamps, the layman Yang Jie dismisses Furong Daokai as merely roaming through such scenery. In the Recorded Sayings of Monk Zhuanyuheng of Purple Bamboo Grove, Zhuanyu Guanheng makes the noun part of a contrast—mountains and waters are “not mountains and waters,” just as people are “not people”—rather than giving it a separate technical definition.

AlternateTargets: Mountains, streams, and all the earth openly display the Buddha’s body
SearchAliases: mountains rivers earth reveal Buddha body

Senses.Note: The line from an older verse says that mountains, rivers, and the whole earth display the Buddha’s body. Later teachers voice it and then point to the ground, raise an object, or ask what is actually being seen. Baiyu warns that merely labeling every visible thing one’s true body is a shallow reading; the line is used to test recognition, not to end the question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 色聲言語。古人恁麼舉揚，雖則盡情分付，爭奈承言者喪、滯句者迷？謂言非道，重重銕壁銀山；謂道是言，忽忽電光石火。進步既乖，退步尤錯，不進不退，自沉自埋。所以向上全提，當機直指，不存一法，不受一塵，無萬行可修，無三界可出，無眾生可度，無諸佛可成。即之如大火輪，不容湊泊；嬰之如吹毛劒，孰敢承當？大徹大悟，對境還迷；有見有聞，觸塗成滯。聲色之前，領略已落二機；語言之後，摶量早遲八刻。與麼則四十九年演說，百千三昧流通，天雨四花，地搖六動，檢點將來，總是色聲言語。畢竟以何為道？若也坐斷要津，別通消息，點出人天眼目，洞照佛祖心肝，如香象之渡河，截流而過；類金毛之出窟，反擲自由。頭頭上明，是體即是用；物物上顯，見色便見心。與麼則山光水影悉露真機，馬呌驢鳴咸宣至理，舉手所指，縱目所觀，聲色語言無往而非道也。然後轉山河為自己，與眾生覿體混融；轉自己歸山河，與諸佛隨緣應現。大眾！即今諸佛、眾生、山河、自己同時變作拂子去也，急著眼看。遂擲下拂子。示眾。山河及大地，全露法王身。草木與叢林，盡作師子吼。舉足下足，入門出門，這邊那邊，築著磕著，好箇現成境界。若到衲僧面前，一點也用不著。所以道，語若迅雷，不容掩耳。機如掣電，豈許停思。八臂那叱搆不來，千眼大悲覰不破。捏得虗空粉碎，依然逼塞乾坤。萬里不掛片雲，青天政好喫棒。千差坐斷，諸佛乞命無由。一線放開，眾生成佛有分。這裏領略得去，方許慶快平生。其或未然，為汝別下註脚。咄。示眾。法無定相，隨念變遷；佛無定形，隨機應化。有時三世諸佛說法，萬象森羅側耳聞；有時萬象森羅說法，三世諸佛立地聽；有時都不恁麼，單單一箇無位真人占斷十方世界，要教萬象森羅無容身之地、三世諸佛無開口之分。這箇境界即今現在目前，山僧路見不平，為他剗却。拈主丈，云：看，看！無位真人墮地來也。擲主丈，下座。浴佛日，示眾。梅雨弄晴，梅風吹濕，悉達太子生也。示拂，云：現在拂子頭上，目顧四方，周行七步，惱亂天下人，盡從今日起。吽！吽！莫道世無雲門，無人敢欺你，惡水驀頭澆，杓柄在老僧手裏。結夏，示眾。護生須是殺，罪犯彌天，殺盡始安居，狼藉不少。惟有生苕帚，功不浪施，掃斷葛藤露布，任諸人坐臥縱橫十二箇時辰，使教顛倒走。與麼則剋期取證，有何消息？薰風自南來，殿閣生微涼。解夏，示眾。以主丈擊禪床，云：圓覺

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 色聲言語。古人恁麼舉揚，雖則盡情分付，爭奈承言者喪、滯句者迷？謂言非道，重重銕壁銀山；謂道是言，忽忽電光石火。進步既乖，退步尤錯，不進不退，自沉自埋。所以向上全提，當機直指，不存一法，不受一塵，無萬行可修，無三界可出，無眾生可度，無諸佛可成。即之如大火輪，不容湊泊；嬰之如吹毛劒，孰敢承當？大徹大悟，對境還迷；有見有聞，觸塗成滯。聲色之前，領略已落二機；語言之後，摶量早遲八刻。與麼則四十九年演說，百千三昧流通，天雨四花，地搖六動，檢點將來，總是色聲言語。畢竟以何為道？若也坐斷要津，別通消息，點出人天眼目，洞照佛祖心肝，如香象之渡河，截流而過；類金毛之出窟，反擲自由。頭頭上明，是體即是用；物物上顯，見色便見心。與麼則山光水影悉露真機，馬呌驢鳴咸宣至理，舉手所指，縱目所觀，聲色語言無往而非道也。然後轉山河為自己，與眾生覿體混融；轉自己歸山河，與諸佛隨緣應現。大眾！即今諸佛、眾生、山河、自己同時變作拂子去也，急著眼看。遂擲下拂子。示眾。山河及大地，全露法王身。草木與叢林，盡作師子吼。舉足下足，入門出門，這邊那邊，築著磕著，好箇現成境界。若到衲僧面前，一點也用不著。所以道，語若迅雷，不容掩耳。機如掣電，豈許停思。八臂那叱搆不來，千眼大悲覰不破。捏得虗空粉碎，依然逼塞乾坤。萬里不掛片雲，青天政好喫棒。千差坐斷，諸佛乞命無由。一線放開，眾生成佛有分。這裏領略得去，方許慶快平生。其或未然，為汝別下註脚。咄。示眾。法無定相，隨念變遷；佛無定形，隨機應化。有時三世諸佛說法，萬象森羅側耳聞；有時萬象森羅說法，三世諸佛立地聽；有時都不恁麼，單單一箇無位真人占斷十方世界，要教萬象森羅無容身之地、三世諸佛無開口之分。這箇境界即今現在目前，山僧路見不平，為他剗却。拈主丈，云：看，看！無位真人墮地來也。擲主丈，下座。浴佛日，示眾。梅雨弄晴，梅風吹濕，悉達太子生也。示拂，云：現在拂子頭上，目顧四方，周行七步，惱亂天下人，盡從今日起。吽！吽！莫道世無雲門，無人敢欺你，惡水驀頭澆，杓柄在老僧手裏。結夏，示眾。護生須是殺，罪犯彌天，殺盡始安居，狼藉不少。惟有生苕帚，功不浪施，掃斷葛藤露布，任諸人坐臥縱橫十二箇時辰，使教顛倒走。與麼則剋期取證，有何消息？薰風自南來，殿閣生微涼。解夏，示眾。以主丈擊禪床，云：圓覺

Senses.Explanation: An older verse declares that the entire visible landscape reveals the Buddha’s body. Tianru voices the line and presses its relevance to the assembly; Faxi speaks it and then lifts his staff. Zishui points to the ground and asks a monk about it; Qiran raises an object to question what is meant by the Buddha’s body. Baiyu warns against merely labeling visible forms, and Zisu raises his staff to ask the assembly where the body is.

Senses.Explanation: Mountains, rivers, and the great earth names the visible landscape and, collectively, the terrestrial world. Huilin Zongben gives the phrase as what lies between heaven and earth, while Sizushan Fayan gives it as the appearance of mind. Luohan Guichen asks whether it is the same as or different from Fayan Wenyi himself; Huangbo Xiyun says it does not go outside the listener's mind; and Baiyun Shouduan says it turns somersaults on the assembly's eyebrows. These are different statements about the same landscape-world expression; they do not make the headword alone carry one metaphysical interpretation.

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 山河天眼裏，世界法身中

Senses.Explanation: Mountains and rivers lie within the heavenly eye; the world lies within the Dharma body. Answer with a vision of the world held in awakened seeing. Fushi Tongxian and Yezhu Fuhui use the complete saying in distinct recorded teaching turns. Hansong Zhicao gives a third current deployment. The spatial image is doctrinal poetry rather than a literal claim about size. Additional distinct current sources: Yezhu Fuhui in J33nB284, Minshu Ruxiang in J39nB450.

Senses.Explanation: The whole landscape is named as the exposed body of the teaching king. Shui’an and Liao’an recite the line in hall addresses; Xiaoyin quotes it and then rejects two abstract explanations offered for it; Wuyi Yuanlai quotes Xiangyan Zhixian’s awakening verse and contrasts it with his own bodily verse. In the first cited passage, Continued Essentials from the Sayings of Ancient Worthies records Shui’an Yan in a direct turn use. In the second cited passage, Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liao’an Qingyu records Liao'an Qingyu in a direct turn use. In the third cited passage, Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xiaoyin Daxin records Xiaoyin Daxin in a direct turn use. In the fourth cited passage, Essentials of the Recorded Sayings of Master Wuyi of Boshan records Xiangyan Zhixian in a quoted-original use, with Wuyi Yuanlai as later quoter and commentator.

Entries.SourceTerm: 山河無隔礙，光明處處透

Senses.PreferredTarget: Mountains and rivers pose no barrier; light shines through everywhere
AlternateTargets: Across mountains and rivers nothing blocks it; its brightness reaches every place
SearchAliases: mountains rivers no barrier light everywhere
Senses.Note: Xuedou's old hall utterance connects the pair with Fu Dashi entering a listener's very nose. Jieshi quotes it and challenges Xuedou's way of addressing the assembly. Yi'an begins a small sermon with the pair and uses his staff to unsettle a merely spatial reading. Yuejiang answers a live question with it; Chushi uses it to interrupt an assembly's quarrel. These are distinct applications of a shared image rather than four recensions of one sermon.

Occurrences.Kwic: 盡目前，紛綸不錯。靠著自己，過患寧無。但不依他作解，何妨顛倒如風。眼孔沒遮攔，腳頭忙蹴踏。八萬四千應手開，滿把珠璣亂拋撒。」拍案一下曰：「劄。」穀日，小參。「一時從地涌出，盡十方世界沒罅子空缺，東來西來、南來北來，不問顆裏幾米、米裏幾顆，一任上載下載、下載上載，肯像他小家子說升合擔石話，忽慢人、限量人。你禪和家聞三下普請鼓，扁擔橫斫不開，箇箇如王氣宇，無論千斛萬斛，一下傾在乂口裏，擔得來始得，擔不來餓殺你。」喝一喝，曰：「我肯小當人。」佛日晦山和尚訃聞，設供，小參。「大統綱宗中事，在風雲不測之中。」喝一喝，曰：「晦山和尚來也，直得乾坤震裂、山岳動搖，見汝諸人不猛著精彩，卻歸佛日寺去也。大眾！一切馳求心歇，無過斯時，佛位、祖位、聖位、賢位、寶几、珍御全不放在眼裏，更說甚三身、四智、五眼、六通？所以直須識句，若不識句，難作箇話會。且如何是句？」復喝一喝，曰：「縱橫展拓氣如王，慧業文章轉法光，提盡古人之未到，始知神化本無方。」小參。「山河無隔礙，光明處處透。拄杖子涌身虛空，穿過南閻浮提、北鬱單越，腳跟下歷過無數坑坎堆阜、土石諸山，還依本位而住。眼前綠水，匹練橫拖；背靠浮圖，一錐迥卓。衲僧道：『我會也。』忽若騎驢入爾缽囊裏、牽牛入爾鞋袋中，身背上知得些子輕重，自不以真如無伎倆，敗闕當風流。」小參。拈起拄杖曰：「熱喫一頓出身白汗了，指望一莖艸上現玉殿瓊樓，那知遭人拶著，卻又擔不出。將山門來燈籠上底手腳，蓋為尋常住在周匝有餘，不解一轉一切轉，如何得著著天地縣殊？即今要與雲門相見，但不遂物意移，自爾雲興雷起。」赴笑隱，臨行，小參。「我意不欲與麼，實是勉勿獲已。」隨拈拄杖，連卓兩卓，曰：「秪在一段一段擔得到人前，不遍於理而適于事，天上人間，乾坤函蓋，萬化千變，逐浪隨波，體淨用明，無流不截。」復卓一卓，曰：「後五日有人領得箇段節要，始知真如不是閒和尚。」翼菴禪師真如語錄卷三小師序璋等記住真如禪寺語錄三小參。「露柱證明，如是我聞。」僧出曰：「收取蝦蟆口不得。」師曰：「一杓臭屎攔面潑。」僧曰：「終不相孤負。」師曰：「露柱證明。」問：「事有形段，短長闊狹隨人看。理無相狀，虛空合喫多少棒？」師曰：「教有明文。」僧曰：「某甲如是。」師曰：「露柱證明。」問：「總上來也是甚麼人？」師曰：「已有名字。」

Occurrences.Kwic: 。僧便問：既是不生不滅，為什麼六道輪迴？峯云：為有心故。僧云：以何方便當證法身？峯云：以虗空心合虗空理。僧云：證後如何？峯云：任從三界轉，徒聽四生奔。復云：會麼？僧云：不會。峯云：禮拜著。師云：九峯大似會作楷法，點畫一一分明。及乎這僧道箇不會，却又拈出草書。雖然，胷中無草書，難看羲獻帖。婺州雲黃山寶林禪寺語錄婺州雲黃山寶林禪寺語錄侍者宗坦延輝編指三門云：此大樓閣無住無去，此樓閣門無開無閉，作者同歸，不勞彈指。彌勒殿，七佛前引，維摩後隨，但知逐隊隨邪，脚跟何曾點地？展坐具，云：看！看！盖地盖天，流通去也。拈帖。一見便見，一得永得。當陽拈出，雷動風行。山門䟽離四句，絕百非，聽取第一義諦。指法座。行到說不到，漏雨漏風；說到行不到，撞墻撞壁。行說俱到時如何？向上有事在。陞座祝聖罷，乃云：擊門槌，拊案尺，遍界刀鏘，參天荊棘。與麼與麼，爐鞴之所；不與麼不與麼，佛手難遮。總不與麼時如何？毗婆尸佛早留心，直至如今不得妙。舉：雪竇明覺禪師示眾云：山河無隔礙，光明處處透。傅大士騎驢入你鼻孔裏，見諸人不惺惺，却歸雙林寺去也。便下座。師云：雪竇與麼說話，要瞞諸人則易，埋沒諸人則難。何故？出門見山水，入門見佛殿。上堂，舉：傅大士帶道冠、儒履、袈裟見梁武帝，帝問云：僧耶？士指冠。帝云：道耶？士指履。帝云：俗耶？士指袈裟。汾陽云：大士多能。五祖戒云：傍觀者醜。師云：武帝高懸聖鑑，要見緇素分明；大士覿面當機，且非索鹽奉馬。檢點將來，只知賣貴，不知賣賤，可惜武帝當時放過，隨後好與一拶。非僧、非道、非俗，又指箇什麼？管取口乾舌大。上堂。一不得向，二不得討。廊下閑行，堂中打坐。眼裏耳裏，觀世音、胡達磨。拍禪床，云：過。結夏，上堂。握驪頷明珠，秉金剛寶劒，日日禁足安居，箇箇心空及第，猶是衲僧尋常行履。雙林乍入院來，不敢背俗違時。下座，且與諸人普同作禮。善慧大士生日，上堂。悲願海，四生海，出沒卷舒，圓融自在。拈拄杖，云：善慧大士來也，石火電光且過一邊，擬欲擡眸，龍華會裏。靠拄杖，下座。上堂：聖制禁足安居，山僧月餘在外。驀嶺㳂山，穿畦透陌。才通大道，又入深村。要過那邊，截流不顧。雖然不遵聖制，却有知音。且道誰是知音？南無心王菩薩。上堂：半夜三更，天昏地黑，赤肉團邊捉得箇賊，正好朝打三千、暮打八百。忽然向白拈手裏分

Occurrences.Kwic: ？師云：趙州東院西。進云：如何是真佛內裏坐？師云：嵩山破竈墮。僧禮拜。師乃云：東邊是知事，西邊是頭首，獅子兒哮吼，龍馬駒𨁝跳。火爐闊一丈，古鏡闊一丈，古佛塔廟前，面南看北斗。臘八，上堂。僧問：半夜逾城時如何？答云：國清才子清，家富小兒嬌。僧云：雪山六年所成者何事？答云：癡人面前不得說夢。僧云：古今皆謂見明星悟道，還諦當也無？答云：一犬吠虗，千猱啀實。師乃云：我觀大地眾生具有如來智慧德相，但以妄想執著而不證得。釋迦老子與麼道，大似蟭螟虫向蚊子眼睫上作窠，向十字街頭叫道：土曠人稀，相逢者少。檢點將來，也是噇酒糟漢。上堂，舉：五祖和尚示眾云：白雲不會說禪，山門開向兩邊。有人動著關捩，兩片東扇西扇。五祖老人盖為慈悲之故，有落草之談。育王不會說禪，屋破覰見青天。等閑從頭盖覆，寧免紙褁麻纏？但願有錢留客醉，也勝騎馬傍人門。上堂，僧問：如何是一生二？師云：元首明，股肱良。進云：如何是二生三？師云：黃河三千年一度清。進云：如何是三生萬物？師云：山河無隔礙，光明處處透。進云：只如新年頭佛法，還有者箇消息也無？師云：樊噲踏鴻門。僧作禮。師乃云：有問新年事，東君總未知，燈籠纔起舞，露柱便掀眉。雪嶺泥牛吼，雲門木馬嘶，樵歌與漁唱，同共樂無為。道濟忠長老通嗣書，上堂：自從胡亂後，三十年不曾少鹽醬，江西信息通也。任你非心非佛，我只是即心即佛，大梅梅子熟也。此乃從上古德風規、叢林榜樣，只如石頭道：書亦不達，信亦不通。又作麼生？有人道得，與你鈯斧子。上堂，舉：僧問五祖：一大藏教是箇切脚，且道切什麼字？祖云：鉢羅娘。應菴問密菴：如何是正法眼？密菴云：破沙盆。師拈云：閩蜀同風，肚裏有虫。到雪竇，眾請上堂，僧問：迅瀑千尋，懸厓萬仞，和尚從什麼處來？答云：官不容針，私通車馬。進云：一日，水空和尚訪大顛和尚，顛把住坐具云：不用通寒暄，不用通來處。此意如何？答云：嶮。進云：水空云：擬欲恁麼，又恐人情不足。還契佗大顛意也無？答云：錦包特石，綿褁蒺䔧。進云：大顛放手云：還足也未？水空提起坐具云：若通時暄，又恐迷來處。大顛云：暫時相見也無妨。又作麼生？答云：虎頭虎尾一時收。進云：只如和尚入山與雪竇和尚相見，較之古人是同是別？答云：竹密不妨流水過，山高豈礙白雲飛？進云：謝師答話。師乃云：向上一路，千聖不傳，釋迦、彌勒仰望

Occurrences.Kwic: 易分雪裡粉，難辨墨中煤。壽山不惜眉毛，從頭注破：一與祖佛為師，分文不直；二驗衲僧眼目，是甚泥彈丸；三與天下人作牓樣，且莫錯會，直饒會得，萬里望鄉關。造萬佛，上堂。僧問：溈山和尚道：凡聖情盡，體露真常。事理不二，即如如佛。即今佛在什麼處？師云：南地竹，北地木。進云：此佛還有形相也無？師云：胡人飲乳，返怪良醫。進云：和尚為什麼特地起模畫樣？師云：打草只要虵驚。進云：未審有功德無功德？師云：放待冷來看。進云：但願東風齊著力，一時吹入我門來。師云：又恁麼去也。乃云：夜夜抱佛眠，喚什麼作佛？朝朝還共起，莫錯認定盤星。起坐鎮相隨，畢竟是阿誰？語默同居止，非一亦非二。纖毫不相離，如身影相似。知這一段虗空，多少人摸索不著。任是精金百煉，巧計千般，鑄也鑄不成，雕也雕不就。傅大士纔開槖籥，便見精神，直得鑑地輝天，騰今耀古。雖然，也祇寫得一半。你諸人從朝至暮，陞堂入戶，開單展鉢，本來面目有甚掩處？還見麼？如今若不究根源，直待當年問彌勒。八月旦，上堂。山河無隔礙，光明處處透。四天下人即今在中庭裏相爭佛法甚閙，忽有箇出來道：諸人幸自無事，無端被野狐涎唾觜邊抹了，見人便要爭佛、爭法，爭這箇、爭那箇，爭到驢年也未歇在。彈指，云：好沒興。天帝釋聞得從三十三天下來，喝云：你這一隊魔子在這裡爭什麼？各與二十棒，貶向他方去也。壽山不覺手之舞之、足之蹈之，火雲初散後，金氣欲涼時。上堂：鴈過長空，影沈寒水。蟲吟古砌，響答虗堂。明明生佛已前，真機獨露。了了見聞不及，覿體無私。坐斷千差，收歸一致。作麼生道？拄杖擬吞三世佛，燈籠百斛瀉明珠。雲溪講主至，上堂：凡夫見色是色、見空是空，聖人見色即空、見空即色。諸人作麼生？若見色是色、見空是空，又同凡夫見；若見色即空、見空即色，又同聖人見。纔有凡聖二見，此人即墮見執，與彼先尼外道無別。驀拈拄杖，云：這箇決定不是色空。作麼生見？令人長憶李將軍，萬里天邊飛一鶚。重陽，上堂。昨日是中秋，今朝又重九，親我紫萸茶，疎他黃菊酒。紫萸與黃菊，本自無踈親，相識滿天下，知心能幾人？怡雲屋造石為佛塔成，上堂，舉：教中道：若人以真金，日施百千兩。不如暫入寺，誠心一禮塔。理上偏枯。若人靜坐一須臾，勝造八萬四千塔。寶塔終久化為塵，一念至心成正覺。事上偏枯。直饒理事雙亡，正偏不立，要見多寶釋迦則未可在

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 盡目前，紛綸不錯。靠著自己，過患寧無。但不依他作解，何妨顛倒如風。眼孔沒遮攔，腳頭忙蹴踏。八萬四千應手開，滿把珠璣亂拋撒。」拍案一下曰：「劄。」穀日，小參。「一時從地涌出，盡十方世界沒罅子空缺，東來西來、南來北來，不問顆裏幾米、米裏幾顆，一任上載下載、下載上載，肯像他小家子說升合擔石話，忽慢人、限量人。你禪和家聞三下普請鼓，扁擔橫斫不開，箇箇如王氣宇，無論千斛萬斛，一下傾在乂口裏，擔得來始得，擔不來餓殺你。」喝一喝，曰：「我肯小當人。」佛日晦山和尚訃聞，設供，小參。「大統綱宗中事，在風雲不測之中。」喝一喝，曰：「晦山和尚來也，直得乾坤震裂、山岳動搖，見汝諸人不猛著精彩，卻歸佛日寺去也。大眾！一切馳求心歇，無過斯時，佛位、祖位、聖位、賢位、寶几、珍御全不放在眼裏，更說甚三身、四智、五眼、六通？所以直須識句，若不識句，難作箇話會。且如何是句？」復喝一喝，曰：「縱橫展拓氣如王，慧業文章轉法光，提盡古人之未到，始知神化本無方。」小參。「山河無隔礙，光明處處透。拄杖子涌身虛空，穿過南閻浮提、北鬱單越，腳跟下歷過無數坑坎堆阜、土石諸山，還依本位而住。眼前綠水，匹練橫拖；背靠浮圖，一錐迥卓。衲僧道：『我會也。』忽若騎驢入爾缽囊裏、牽牛入爾鞋袋中，身背上知得些子輕重，自不以真如無伎倆，敗闕當風流。」小參。拈起拄杖曰：「熱喫一頓出身白汗了，指望一莖艸上現玉殿瓊樓，那知遭人拶著，卻又擔不出。將山門來燈籠上底手腳，蓋為尋常住在周匝有餘，不解一轉一切轉，如何得著著天地縣殊？即今要與雲門相見，但不遂物意移，自爾雲興雷起。」赴笑隱，臨行，小參。「我意不欲與麼，實是勉勿獲已。」隨拈拄杖，連卓兩卓，曰：「秪在一段一段擔得到人前，不遍於理而適于事，天上人間，乾坤函蓋，萬化千變，逐浪隨波，體淨用明，無流不截。」復卓一卓，曰：「後五日有人領得箇段節要，始知真如不是閒和尚。」翼菴禪師真如語錄卷三小師序璋等記住真如禪寺語錄三小參。「露柱證明，如是我聞。」僧出曰：「收取蝦蟆口不得。」師曰：「一杓臭屎攔面潑。」僧曰：「終不相孤負。」師曰：「露柱證明。」問：「事有形段，短長闊狹隨人看。理無相狀，虛空合喫多少棒？」師曰：「教有明文。」僧曰：「某甲如是。」師曰：「露柱證明。」問：「總上來也是甚麼人？」師曰：「已有名字。」

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 。僧便問：既是不生不滅，為什麼六道輪迴？峯云：為有心故。僧云：以何方便當證法身？峯云：以虗空心合虗空理。僧云：證後如何？峯云：任從三界轉，徒聽四生奔。復云：會麼？僧云：不會。峯云：禮拜著。師云：九峯大似會作楷法，點畫一一分明。及乎這僧道箇不會，却又拈出草書。雖然，胷中無草書，難看羲獻帖。婺州雲黃山寶林禪寺語錄婺州雲黃山寶林禪寺語錄侍者宗坦延輝編指三門云：此大樓閣無住無去，此樓閣門無開無閉，作者同歸，不勞彈指。彌勒殿，七佛前引，維摩後隨，但知逐隊隨邪，脚跟何曾點地？展坐具，云：看！看！盖地盖天，流通去也。拈帖。一見便見，一得永得。當陽拈出，雷動風行。山門䟽離四句，絕百非，聽取第一義諦。指法座。行到說不到，漏雨漏風；說到行不到，撞墻撞壁。行說俱到時如何？向上有事在。陞座祝聖罷，乃云：擊門槌，拊案尺，遍界刀鏘，參天荊棘。與麼與麼，爐鞴之所；不與麼不與麼，佛手難遮。總不與麼時如何？毗婆尸佛早留心，直至如今不得妙。舉：雪竇明覺禪師示眾云：山河無隔礙，光明處處透。傅大士騎驢入你鼻孔裏，見諸人不惺惺，却歸雙林寺去也。便下座。師云：雪竇與麼說話，要瞞諸人則易，埋沒諸人則難。何故？出門見山水，入門見佛殿。上堂，舉：傅大士帶道冠、儒履、袈裟見梁武帝，帝問云：僧耶？士指冠。帝云：道耶？士指履。帝云：俗耶？士指袈裟。汾陽云：大士多能。五祖戒云：傍觀者醜。師云：武帝高懸聖鑑，要見緇素分明；大士覿面當機，且非索鹽奉馬。檢點將來，只知賣貴，不知賣賤，可惜武帝當時放過，隨後好與一拶。非僧、非道、非俗，又指箇什麼？管取口乾舌大。上堂。一不得向，二不得討。廊下閑行，堂中打坐。眼裏耳裏，觀世音、胡達磨。拍禪床，云：過。結夏，上堂。握驪頷明珠，秉金剛寶劒，日日禁足安居，箇箇心空及第，猶是衲僧尋常行履。雙林乍入院來，不敢背俗違時。下座，且與諸人普同作禮。善慧大士生日，上堂。悲願海，四生海，出沒卷舒，圓融自在。拈拄杖，云：善慧大士來也，石火電光且過一邊，擬欲擡眸，龍華會裏。靠拄杖，下座。上堂：聖制禁足安居，山僧月餘在外。驀嶺㳂山，穿畦透陌。才通大道，又入深村。要過那邊，截流不顧。雖然不遵聖制，却有知音。且道誰是知音？南無心王菩薩。上堂：半夜三更，天昏地黑，赤肉團邊捉得箇賊，正好朝打三千、暮打八百。忽然向白拈手裏分

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 易分雪裡粉，難辨墨中煤。壽山不惜眉毛，從頭注破：一與祖佛為師，分文不直；二驗衲僧眼目，是甚泥彈丸；三與天下人作牓樣，且莫錯會，直饒會得，萬里望鄉關。造萬佛，上堂。僧問：溈山和尚道：凡聖情盡，體露真常。事理不二，即如如佛。即今佛在什麼處？師云：南地竹，北地木。進云：此佛還有形相也無？師云：胡人飲乳，返怪良醫。進云：和尚為什麼特地起模畫樣？師云：打草只要虵驚。進云：未審有功德無功德？師云：放待冷來看。進云：但願東風齊著力，一時吹入我門來。師云：又恁麼去也。乃云：夜夜抱佛眠，喚什麼作佛？朝朝還共起，莫錯認定盤星。起坐鎮相隨，畢竟是阿誰？語默同居止，非一亦非二。纖毫不相離，如身影相似。知這一段虗空，多少人摸索不著。任是精金百煉，巧計千般，鑄也鑄不成，雕也雕不就。傅大士纔開槖籥，便見精神，直得鑑地輝天，騰今耀古。雖然，也祇寫得一半。你諸人從朝至暮，陞堂入戶，開單展鉢，本來面目有甚掩處？還見麼？如今若不究根源，直待當年問彌勒。八月旦，上堂。山河無隔礙，光明處處透。四天下人即今在中庭裏相爭佛法甚閙，忽有箇出來道：諸人幸自無事，無端被野狐涎唾觜邊抹了，見人便要爭佛、爭法，爭這箇、爭那箇，爭到驢年也未歇在。彈指，云：好沒興。天帝釋聞得從三十三天下來，喝云：你這一隊魔子在這裡爭什麼？各與二十棒，貶向他方去也。壽山不覺手之舞之、足之蹈之，火雲初散後，金氣欲涼時。上堂：鴈過長空，影沈寒水。蟲吟古砌，響答虗堂。明明生佛已前，真機獨露。了了見聞不及，覿體無私。坐斷千差，收歸一致。作麼生道？拄杖擬吞三世佛，燈籠百斛瀉明珠。雲溪講主至，上堂：凡夫見色是色、見空是空，聖人見色即空、見空即色。諸人作麼生？若見色是色、見空是空，又同凡夫見；若見色即空、見空即色，又同聖人見。纔有凡聖二見，此人即墮見執，與彼先尼外道無別。驀拈拄杖，云：這箇決定不是色空。作麼生見？令人長憶李將軍，萬里天邊飛一鶚。重陽，上堂。昨日是中秋，今朝又重九，親我紫萸茶，疎他黃菊酒。紫萸與黃菊，本自無踈親，相識滿天下，知心能幾人？怡雲屋造石為佛塔成，上堂，舉：教中道：若人以真金，日施百千兩。不如暫入寺，誠心一禮塔。理上偏枯。若人靜坐一須臾，勝造八萬四千塔。寶塔終久化為塵，一念至心成正覺。事上偏枯。直饒理事雙亡，正偏不立，要見多寶釋迦則未可在

Tianyin Yuanxiu gives it to an abrupt demand; Wufeng Ruxue's attendant gives it when asked the ancestral meaning, and Wufeng challenges where he learned that empty talk. Senses.Explanation: This landscape saying pictures clouds crossing open air unhindered by the mountain’s height. Chan masters repeatedly speak it, paired with dense bamboo not blocking water, as a public answer. The records quote it after “dense bamboo does not prevent flowing water,” deploy it as an answer, and also challenge speakers who merely repeat it. The cited passages span 5 works and preserve the exact headword in the quoted Chinese. The gloss reports the shared use and leaves each surrounding case to its own recorded exchange.

Senses.Explanation: The stride of the leaving: retreat done, gold wind in the leaves, the brothers go east and west. Dongshan's stock line sends them to where not an inch of grass grows in ten thousand li, Shishuang answers that out the gate is grass — and every generation warns the leaver what waits on the road. Senses.Explanation: A death in one household causes mourning in another. The saying turns a neighbor's grief into a question about who is involved in an event and why. The selected masters use it as diagnosis, direct answer, and a question answered by an enacted cry.

Senses.PreferredTarget: someone dies in the eastern house and the western house joins the mourning
SearchAliases: someone dies in the eastern house and the western house joins the mourning
Senses.Note: Someone dies in the eastern house and the western household joins the mourning, a household-to-household scene retained across the cited addresses. AlternateTargets: the East Mountain walks upon the water
SearchAliases: East Mountain walks on water case
Senses.Explanation: East Mountain walks on water is Yunmen Wenyan's answer when asked where the buddhas emerge. Yunmen's own recorded sayings preserve the exchange directly. Yuanwu Keqin includes the saying among several expressions that he says are pierced through on one string; Dahui Zonggao also recounts Yuanwu raising Yunmen's exchange and answering the same question with ‘The fragrant wind comes from the south; the halls give rise to a slight coolness.’ An unnamed monk asks Chaozong Tongren for the saying's import, and Chaozong replies, ‘In the heap of fierce flames, the moon always shines.’ Tianran Hanshi quotes Yunmen's answer in a verse and says that the conversational thread has been transmitted to the present. These passages preserve, quote, question, answer, and versify the sentence, but do not supply a stable paraphrase of how the mountain walks.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense covers Yunmen's answer and its later use as a case-saying. Literally, East Mountain (東山) walks or goes (行) upon the water (水上).

Senses.Explanation: The second half of Yunmen's fan saying: the fan leaps to the Thirty-Three Heavens and staves in Sakra's nostril — a carp of the eastern sea takes one blow, and the rain pours like a basin. Held up at drought-time, swapped onto a staff, judged wrong three times over. The saying recited and tested: Yushan Shangsi springs the fan up — see, see! the fan leaps to the heavens, touches Sakra's nostril, the eastern-sea carp takes its blow, the rain like a basin pouring — I am used to holding this true word, he says, is there anyone to receive and live it? Only bring a willing mind and it will not cheat you; Yulin Tongxiu at the evening sitting has the lame teacher say it and asks whether it really is so; the monk's answer misses — no wonder the world is in drought, he rules, and goes back to his room; Dahui Zonggao answers the needle-and-horse-cart exchange by reciting it whole — and what then? — and when the monk answers in high style, dismisses it as a fart set to the Great Stone tune; Muchen Daomin raises it at the evening sitting and sets Qianyan's counter beside it: the fan leaps into the eighteenfold hells, strikes the King of Death on the nose, the king rages — you have eaten your share of congee and rice; Dahui again, where tracking cannot track and words cannot speak: Yunmen's fan in hand still leaps and strikes, the carp still takes its blow, the rain still pours — what, after all, is the purport? A shout. The blow moved onto the staff: Miyun Yuanwu rules the staff may be used as the sixteen-foot golden body and the golden body as the staff — then the staff-child leaps to the heavens, touches Sakra's nostril, the carp takes its blow, the rain pours: do not any of you go hide in the old temple — one blow will break your donkey's back; Tianyin Yuanxiu dawns to a single chestnut-wood staff left over — held crosswise, used upside down, all fitting — one touch touches Sakra's nostril, the carp takes its blow, the rain like a basin pouring, and someone asks whether that is Yunmen's fan and not Deshan's staff; Tian'an Sheng runs rivers and sea — what does the river say? the dragon-and-snake dwell there; what does the sea say? the treasure-store rises there; what do I say? — the staff-child leaps to the heavens, the carp takes its blow, the rain pours; and asked which canon this clause comes from, he laughs: the benevolent see it and call it benevolence.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Strike the carp in the eastern sea once, and rain pours as if from a basin
AlternateTargets: Give the East Sea carp one blow; rain comes down in sheets
SearchAliases: East Sea carp one strike rain pours basin Yunmen
strike carp eastern sea torrential rain Chan
Senses.Note: The carp and rain image belongs to a wider Yunmen fan saying. Tianyin criticizes a later repetition of it; Miyun and Shiqi recast it with their own staffs. Zhe'an uses the pair in a sermon invoking rain, Yuan'an sets the fan half aside, and Chulin substitutes a pillow. These separate current uses give the pair a job of its own, while the two shorter public headwords remain its component images.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 玉砌樓臺，重重珠網張施其上，種種寶蓮圍繞其中，塗香散花芬瑩崇麗，樹林水鳥各演妙音，說一切眾生往劫所行廣大善根、說一切諸佛疇昔所行廣大利益，有如是莊嚴、有如是境界，彌陀未降生也不曾缺一隅、彌陀既出世也不曾增一角，十分坦蕩、八面玲瓏，人人到此躊躇顧慮，把手拽伊不入，以至終身淪棄。」驀豎拂子，曰：「無量壽尊坐視不安。向拂子頭上口喃喃，曰：『善男子會也麼？曾有志，莫蹉跎，兩丸拋擲如梭，舊路多岐不可戀，前賢捷徑好橫趨，要作堂堂美丈夫，誠孚一念妄情枯，何必在隔江招手，重畫麒麟閣上圖？』」乃擊拂子一下。上堂。「山僧昔年胡行亂撞，毒刺傷足，痛入骨髓，便矢願不做者般蟲豸，擬縮在茅茨土窟裏，髮長貌醜，一任時人檢點。不期逼上俳場，終日忙忙碌碌，夜裏脫襪子，忽然抓著舊時痛處，惶恐無地。特將此段因緣普告大眾，不得作佛法揣摩、不得作世諦計較，若有痛癢相關底，不妨出來商量。」良久，曰：「可惜蓋世金章，寫作尋常閒話。」祈雨，上堂。「扇子𨁝跳上天，築著帝釋鼻孔；東海鯉魚打一棒，雨似盆傾。雲門老子費力太多，見功實少。顯聖者裏，人人奮不退轉心、箇箇立決定志，佛殿裏燒香、山門頭合掌，梵音響處雷震晴空，法語宣時雨傾大地，便見三艸二木意氣揚揚，敗種焦芽生機勃勃。山僧聲氣不動，但喝彩有分。」良久，曰：「應節慈雲看靉靆，豐年全得雨滂沱。」上堂。橫按拄杖，曰：「在古非先，居今不後。三相勿得推遷，二鼠無因攢齧。提持千聖，千聖類他不齊；出生諸佛，諸佛混他不得。水國煙村，將空王如來鼻孔橫穿；花街柳巷，把彌勒大士面門剺破。揮慧日以當天，響真風於遍界。所以令一切眾生斷除障礙、令一切眾生堅固善根、令一切眾生裂破慳囊、令一切眾生勤種福田、令一切眾生捨邊邪路、令一切眾生入正覺門，同真俗、徹始終，窮源極流，莫一與二，浩然大均，名曰拄杖。更說甚麼禾山鼓、雪峰毬，塵擾擾、鬧啾啾，不若一齊放下休。」遂擲拄杖。長至，上堂。「迷悟不異，動靜一源。進不上前，退不落後。坐萬年床，斟無為酒。隨心飲啄，適意絃歌。人人道曲肱高枕，樂在其中。豈知正是生死岸頭事。」拈拂子畫一畫，曰：「向者裏推坍鐵壁，趯倒銀山。直陞堂奧，別展化機。一陽飛葭管之灰，四海濟成平之運。小人從茲革面，君子得以暢懷。或現尊特身，慈御萬方。或現異類身，悲援群有。隴上寒梅，皆含霽色；溪邊古木，

Senses.Explanation: This is movement without a fixed emergence point: rising here and disappearing there, then reversing or shifting the same pattern across the other directions. Linji expands the east-west pair into south-north, middle-edge, and edge-middle movement; Yuan’an Liao gives the phrase within an image of forms appearing throughout the world, while Beita Siguang uses it in an answer to an unnamed questioner. Hanyue Fazang then tests whether anyone can speak from the place of such movement.

Senses.Explanation: Water flows through the eastern and western ravines; clouds rise over the southern and northern mountains. The paired landscape answers Chan questions through ordinary water and clouds, making the immediate scene carry the teaching turn. Four current Tier-2 deployments by Erzhan Zun, Yune Xi, Hanxiu, and Pufuzhuo. Erzhan and Pufuzhuo give it as a present answer, Yune Xi uses it only to demand a further test, and Hanxiu makes it his own verse on an old case. The sources deploy this as an answer and verse image; no fixed geographical claim or single doctrinal formula is implied.

Senses.Explanation: The Eastern Rank is an institutional group in a Chan monastery. The monastic rules place it opposite the Western Rank and direct its members during formal ceremonies. Gulin Qingmao addresses the administrative officers of the Eastern Rank. A Lantern Festival heading thanks the hall custodian of the Eastern Rank and Wunian Xitang as two separately formed designations; Xitang is Wunian's title there, not a matching western rank. The Outline Record later transmits the same heading.

Senses.Explanation: Going east leaves the advantage of going west unseen. Yunju Xiaoshun answers his interlocutor's displayed purchase with this directional rebuke, while Yuanwu Keqin, Mi'an Xianjie, and later commentators reuse it to expose one-sided handling. The sentence contrasts an eastward course with the benefit visible from the west. Linquan Conglun joins it to the complaint that a clever person's work is disliked by the clumsy; Baoning Renyong pairs it with prices differing north and south.

Senses.Explanation: Unable to distinguish east from west or north from south describes complete loss of directional distinction. Sanyi Mingyu rhetorically mixes the regions into one mass; Bulin Zongjian imagines a person arriving after conceptual barriers collapse; Yikui Yuankui recounts severe first-person disorientation; and an unnamed monk uses the phrase in a question to Linwo Jian. Wuwen Daocan uses the same pair in a separate warning that such directionless people invite encroachment on their boundaries. Xifeng Huo gives it as a direct answer about the time before the sun rises, a separate use from Wuwen's warning.

Senses.Explanation: The eastern and western halls are the two institutional divisions of the monastic community. Monastic records speak of the head monks of the two halls giving formal addresses, and regulations direct the two halls during ceremonies. In Nanquan's cat case, the phrase names these two groups—or their leaders—not an Eastern Rank paired with a Western Rank. It occurs throughout later treatments of the case: the eastern and western halls dispute over a cat, Nanquan demands a word that will save it, and the assembly does not answer.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB189.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Yu. Sanyi raises his whisk and says that, with no other choice, he is treating a dead horse. He gives the paired dimensions, then overturns the expected scale with Mount Sumeru planted upside down, the four seas displaced, cooking at the top of a monastery pole, and three monkeys tossing coins at night. The headword is part of Sanyi's own brief address, not an itinerary or a monk's question. Its wide span is immediately put into a sequence of impossible images; the source offers no conversion of the numbers into a measurable distance. The next address begins with wind and sudden rain.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB394.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yi’an. On the Buddha's awakening day, a monk asks Yi'an to account for the morning star piercing the eye. Yi'an answers with the headword. The monk concludes that saving beings is already finished, but Yi'an continues by speaking of grasping the true and of forms remaining clearly present; later he asks how such displays are understood in their substance. He raises his whisk and depicts Shakyamuni's radiance, then drops it and ends with an eye-film producing a shower of imaginary flowers. The paired numbers are Yi'an's first answer in this exchange, not a reported measurement of the star or automatic confirmation of the monk's conclusion.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB464.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qizongzhen (Huayan). At Qizong's opening address, a monk asks Jinshan's age in the context of heaven and earth sharing a root. Qizong answers with the numbers. Asked his own age, he says it is no different from Jinshan's; the monk supplies a moon-and-sky couplet and is warned not to misunderstand, then receives a blow whose status as reward or punishment is itself questioned. In his ensuing address Qizong repeats the headword after saying that the assembly may understand; if they do not, he offers the same moon-and-sky couplet as a footnote. Thus the first use is an answer about age and the second belongs to his current instruction. Neither is a literal age calculation.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB365.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shipuzhi. At the completion of precept conferral on the Buddha's awakening day, a monk asks Shipu: if the Buddha never spoke one word in forty-nine years, from where do Chan and precepts arise? Shipu answers with the headword. The monk responds with one flower opening five petals and fruit naturally ripening; Shipu says the monk has voiced it. Further questions examine the morning star and awakening from other angles before Shipu's address criticizes easy accounts of seeing the star. The numbers are his reply to the question about the two traditions' origin, not a chronology of forty-nine years or a claim about their geographical separation.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB386.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuan’an Feng. At the commemoration of Tiantong Miyun, a monk asks Yuan'an how one can act apart from mind, intention, and consciousness if the three worlds are mind's work. Yuan'an answers with the headword. Asked whether it is mind or not mind, he allows the questioner to go on with divination. His address then questions attempts to identify the ancestor through grand comparisons, gestures, or doctrinal alternatives, before returning to the descendants' present offering of incense and food. The paired dimensions are a current answer within that challenge, not an anatomical or geographical account of mind. The commemorated teacher is a different speaker layer from Yuan'an.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB450.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Minshu. At Minshu's arrival at Baizhang monastery, the record places the headword in his statement at the mountain gate. He follows it by saying that his coming here involves no petty complication. Pointing his staff at the gate, he says every gate has a road to the capital and every place is a teaching banner, then enters. The Buddha-hall statements, taking the abbot's room, ascent to the seat, and incense offerings come afterward as separately marked ceremonial acts. The headword is Minshu's arrival formula, with its broad directions brought immediately into the present gate; it does not give the route or mileage of his journey.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB488.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dounan Wei. In Dounan's remembered visit to Xuedou, Hongyuan asks where he has come from and tests him with questions about the stone bridge and a true message. Dounan lowers his head to drink tea. Hongyuan then asks about a cup falling and a saucer breaking into seven pieces; Dounan replies with the paired dimensions. The record next recounts a later incident while Dounan serves as tea steward, including a shout, a blow, and a question about reward and punishment. The headword is Dounan's answer to Hongyuan in the first tea encounter, not Hongyuan's own pronouncement or part of that later incident.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB189.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Yu. Sanyi raises his whisk and says that, with no other choice, he is treating a dead horse. He gives the paired dimensions, then overturns the expected scale with Mount Sumeru planted upside down, the four seas displaced, cooking at the top of a monastery pole, and three monkeys tossing coins at night. The headword is part of Sanyi's own brief address, not an itinerary or a monk's question. Its wide span is immediately put into a sequence of impossible images; the source offers no conversion of the numbers into a measurable distance. The next address begins with wind and sudden rain.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB394.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yi’an. On the Buddha's awakening day, a monk asks Yi'an to account for the morning star piercing the eye. Yi'an answers with the headword. The monk concludes that saving beings is already finished, but Yi'an continues by speaking of grasping the true and of forms remaining clearly present; later he asks how such displays are understood in their substance. He raises his whisk and depicts Shakyamuni's radiance, then drops it and ends with an eye-film producing a shower of imaginary flowers. The paired numbers are Yi'an's first answer in this exchange, not a reported measurement of the star or automatic confirmation of the monk's conclusion.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB464.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qizongzhen (Huayan). At Qizong's opening address, a monk asks Jinshan's age in the context of heaven and earth sharing a root. Qizong answers with the numbers. Asked his own age, he says it is no different from Jinshan's; the monk supplies a moon-and-sky couplet and is warned not to misunderstand, then receives a blow whose status as reward or punishment is itself questioned. In his ensuing address Qizong repeats the headword after saying that the assembly may understand; if they do not, he offers the same moon-and-sky couplet as a footnote. Thus the first use is an answer about age and the second belongs to his current instruction. Neither is a literal age calculation.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB365.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shipuzhi. At the completion of precept conferral on the Buddha's awakening day, a monk asks Shipu: if the Buddha never spoke one word in forty-nine years, from where do Chan and precepts arise? Shipu answers with the headword. The monk responds with one flower opening five petals and fruit naturally ripening; Shipu says the monk has voiced it. Further questions examine the morning star and awakening from other angles before Shipu's address criticizes easy accounts of seeing the star. The numbers are his reply to the question about the two traditions' origin, not a chronology of forty-nine years or a claim about their geographical separation.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB386.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuan’an Feng. At the commemoration of Tiantong Miyun, a monk asks Yuan'an how one can act apart from mind, intention, and consciousness if the three worlds are mind's work. Yuan'an answers with the headword. Asked whether it is mind or not mind, he allows the questioner to go on with divination. His address then questions attempts to identify the ancestor through grand comparisons, gestures, or doctrinal alternatives, before returning to the descendants' present offering of incense and food. The paired dimensions are a current answer within that challenge, not an anatomical or geographical account of mind. The commemorated teacher is a different speaker layer from Yuan'an.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB450.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Minshu. At Minshu's arrival at Baizhang monastery, the record places the headword in his statement at the mountain gate. He follows it by saying that his coming here involves no petty complication. Pointing his staff at the gate, he says every gate has a road to the capital and every place is a teaching banner, then enters. The Buddha-hall statements, taking the abbot's room, ascent to the seat, and incense offerings come afterward as separately marked ceremonial acts. The headword is Minshu's arrival formula, with its broad directions brought immediately into the present gate; it does not give the route or mileage of his journey.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB488.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dounan Wei. In Dounan's remembered visit to Xuedou, Hongyuan asks where he has come from and tests him with questions about the stone bridge and a true message. Dounan lowers his head to drink tea. Hongyuan then asks about a cup falling and a saucer breaking into seven pieces; Dounan replies with the paired dimensions. The record next recounts a later incident while Dounan serves as tea steward, including a shout, a blow, and a question about reward and punishment. The headword is Dounan's answer to Hongyuan in the first tea encounter, not Hongyuan's own pronouncement or part of that later incident.

Senses.Explanation: A hundred thousand east and west, eight thousand north and south: the paired numbers spread across both axes without specifying a unit or a place to measure. Their local force varies. Sanyi sets them amid impossible inversions after raising his whisk; Yi'an answers a challenge about the Buddha's awakening; Qizong uses them both in a question about Jinshan's age and again in his own address. Shipu applies them to a question about the origins of Chan and precepts, Yuan'an to a question beyond ordinary mind and cognition, and Minshu to arriving at the monastery gate. In Dounan's record they are his reply during a remembered encounter over tea with Xuedou. The notes explain those actual turns rather than treating the numbers as a map or a fixed symbolic quantity. The expression can interrupt a question's expected scale or frame, but each speaker's next words or action determine what is being tested.

Senses.Explanation: Four graphs that sweep the whole of space, and the masters who swing them loose from geography. Yunmen Wenyan answers winter's passing with a staff carried across the shoulders and free wandering in all quarters, Fenyang Shanzhao pictures the seeker crossing frost and snow through all quarters to cut the one thing in two, Xuedou Chongxian holds the staff sideways in his own hand and asks where the quartered world comes from, Hongzhi Zhengjue sets responding with no fixed direction against the life and death bred inside the board of the quarters, and Dahui Zonggao answers the tree-bare leaves-fall case with all quarters, four diagonals, and above and below. Baiyun Shouduan looses Zhaozhou's falcon through ten-thousand-mile clouds to bolt in any quarter, Chushi Fanqi meets the clay-Buddha question with all quarters and one hundred and eight thousand, Yulin Tongxiu fills the seamless hall to bursting with the moon wheel red in every quarter, Yunwai Xingze rolls hall inside and outside into one piece and kneads the quarters flat and round, and Konggu Daocheng splits the primal mass into the two modes and branches it into the quarters of myriad worlds.

Senses.Explanation: Zen masters use this profitable market transaction both to present command of circumstances and to expose calculation. Zhufeng Fa says that when conditions mature one can buy cheap at the east end and sell dear at the west end, freely turn black and yellow, and seize the market. Zhulang Chesheng places the maxim amid explicit talk of buying, selling, profit, and loss before contrasting commercial seekers with Chan practitioners. Po'an Zuxian puts the transaction on the market scale and calls the result repeatedly mistaken. Haiyin Zhaoru compares Dongshan Kong's adjustments to buying cheap and selling dear, then says that the prices do not tally and the bargain is incomplete. The transaction remains the same in each case: advantageous dealing across the market. What changes is the verdict—command in one setting, commercial calculation in another.

Senses.Explanation: To construe the words is repeatedly rejected when a hearer turns an answer, gesture, or ordinary statement into a fixed verbal interpretation. In Chan records it repeatedly names an auditor's reduction of a reply or case to an explanatory category. Yuanwu reports that people construe Dongshan's 'three pounds of hemp' as an answer based on his work weighing hemp; Dahui says blind fellows construe Zhaozhou's instruction as merely 'wash the bowl'; and Fayan says that for twenty years he construed Jiashan's line only as talk about scenery. The records also expose competing constructions: a collection says people construed Vimalakirti's response as silence, a pause, remaining seated, or not answering, but none reached it. Guyin Yuncong can therefore warn, after answering 'what is buddha?', 'do not construe it as answer-buddha talk.' Elsewhere the word is itself put under interview pressure: 'without relying on the three-inch tongue, try to construe it.' The Chan-specific bend is observable and critical: construing the words (話會) is not neutral comprehension but the named act of fitting a live saying into talk about a subject. The entry does not decide what an unexplained saying ultimately means.

Senses.Note: Feiyin faults a monk for failing to catch even his own preceding turn. Yinyuan says the line after a monk’s shout and hesitation; Tian’an says it after a verse about an unchanging pine; Eryin says it when a monk cannot say what “one” means in “the myriad things return to one.” Huanglian, Mixing, Yushan, and Cuiya likewise use it against answers or shouts that miss their particular questions. The “head of the talk” is the point of the encounter at hand. The old Sansheng rebuke to Xuefeng is a related full saying, but these are later masters’ fresh, direct uses.

Senses.Explanation: A master says this when the student’s reply fails to meet the live question already on the floor. Feiyin, Yinyuan, Tian’an, and Eryin use the line to stop a move that ignores the question or the master’s immediately preceding words. Huanglian, Mixing, Yushan, and Cuiya use it in further interviews where a stock phrase or shout has not answered the particular challenge.
